---
title: "A2 exercises — Feeding, metabolism and temperature"
---

Use the [tutorial](index.qmd). All numerical observations below are invented
teaching examples. This is analysis of supplied information, not an animal
handling or respirometry protocol. Allow 60–90 minutes. Leave with a labelled
energy budget, rate calculations and one mechanistic comparison.

## 1. Follow a meal

Trace a starch molecule from ingestion to absorbed sugar and subsequent ATP
production in an animal cell. Distinguish mechanical processing, hydrolysis,
membrane transport and cellular metabolism. Where does the gut lumen sit
relative to the internal environment?

Compare a foregut fermenter with a hindgut fermenter. Why do microbial
location and retention time matter? Give one benefit and one cost/trade-off
of microbial fermentation without claiming one arrangement is always best.

## 2. Make the energy account balance

For one animal over one day, supplied values are ingested energy 150 kJ,
faecal loss 40 kJ, chemical energy excreted 10 kJ and metabolic expenditure
85 kJ. Calculate retained energy, and express metabolic expenditure as a
mean power in watts over that day. Use 1 kJ = 1,000 J and 1 day = 86,400 s.

What changes if metabolic expenditure becomes 110 kJ with other terms held
fixed? Explain the biological meaning of a negative retained balance. State
why neither budget alone proves whether protein supply was adequate.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint

Use the same time interval for every energy term. Watts are J s⁻¹, not kJ day⁻¹.
:::

## 3. Calculate and compare oxygen-use rates

A hypothetical 0.20 L water chamber is followed for 10 min. Oxygen decline
for an empty-chamber blank over the same interval is 0.05 mg L⁻¹.
Each row below represents a different animal in its own chamber; all animals
have mass 2.0 g. Conditions other than the labelled temperature are stipulated
to be comparable for this arithmetic exercise.

| Animal | Temperature (°C) | Oxygen decline (mg L⁻¹ per 10 min) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| C1 | 10 | 0.25 |
| C2 | 10 | 0.30 |
| W1 | 20 | 0.45 |
| W2 | 20 | 0.55 |

Calculate blank-corrected oxygen consumption in mg min⁻¹ and then
mg min⁻¹ g⁻¹ for each animal. Find the mean rate at each temperature and
the apparent $Q_{10}$ from those means. Show one full row calculation.

What is the independent experimental unit? Would ten sensor readings from
C1 increase the number of independent animals? Explain why the two animals
per condition and stipulated design provide limited biological evidence.

## 4. Read the temperature mechanism

An ectotherm has increasing oxygen consumption from 10 to 20 °C. An insulated
endotherm has increasing resting oxygen consumption as air cools from 15 to
5 °C. Explain how both observations can occur without contradiction. State
which body-temperature measurements would help distinguish the mechanisms.

Why should a measured $Q_{10}$ not be used to predict performance at any
temperature? Name two conditions other than temperature that should be checked.

## 5. Connect gut histology to function

Sketch an idealised intestinal villus and label lumen, absorptive epithelium,
underlying support and internal transport route. Predict the consequences
of reducing absorptive area while keeping diet and other conditions fixed.
Then state what your sketch cannot establish about an actual section's organ
identity or physiological performance.

## 6. Design an interpretation, not a new method

Write a short results paragraph for task 3 giving direction, size, units,
replicate count and one physiological explanation. Follow it with one limitation
and a proposed improvement. Do not claim that mass normalisation removes all
size effects, or that oxygen consumption measures every contribution to ATP
supply during rapid activity.

Check your concepts with the [quiz](quiz.qmd).
